questions.question: In a party hall, there are people in blue and red dresses. The ratio of number of men in blue to the number of Women in red is 3 ∶ 7, The ratio of men in red to the number of women in blue is 2 ∶ 1. If the ratio of number of people in blue to the number of people in red is 35 ∶ 76, then what is the ratio of number of men to the number of women?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Ratio of Men in blue (M_b) to Women in red (W_r): 3 ∶ 7

Ratio of Men in red (M_r) to Women in blue (W_b): 2 ∶ 1 

Ratio of People in blue (P_b) to People in red (P_r): 35 ∶ 76

**Solution:**

Men in Blue (MB) = 3x

Women in Red (WR) = 7x

Men in Red (MR) = 2y

Women in Blue (WB) = y

People in Blue (PB) = Men in Blue + Women in Blue = 3x + y

People in Red (PR) = Men in Red + Women in Red = 2y + 7x

(3x + y)/(7x + 2y) = 35/76

76(3x + y) = 35(7x + 2y)

228x + 76y = 245x + 70y

17x = 6y

x = 6y/17 ----(1)

Men = MB + MR = 3x + 2y = 3(6y/17) + 2y = 18y/17 + 2y

Women = WR + WB = 7x + y = 7(6y/17) + y = 42y/17 + y

Men/Women = (18y/17 + 2y)/(42y/17 + y)

(18y + 34y)/(42y + 17y)

Men/Women = 52/59

**So, the ratio of men to women is 52 : 59.**

questions.question:
The pie chart given below shows the number of employees in 6 different companies. The total number of employees in all these 6 companies 15840. The number of employees in a particular company is shown in terms of degree with respect to the total number of employees in all these 6 companies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a63ce739ce11143445c96157fbfd6395c1801194ea4d62080b571c97e735eda5.png] 

J1 = The total number of employees in P, Q, S, T, and U.

J2 = The difference between the total number of employees in P and Q and the total number of employees in T and U.

What is the value of (J1 + J2)?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

J1 = The total number of employees in P, Q, S, T, and U.

77° + 103° + 40° + 81° + 20° = 321°

J2 = The difference between the total number of employees in P and Q and the total number of employees in T and U.

P + Q = 77° + 103° = 180°

T + U = 40° + 20° = 60°

J2 = 180° - 60° = 120°

(J1 + J2) = 321° + 120° = 441°

360° = 15840

1° = 44

441° = 44 × 441 = 19404

**∴ Option 1 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: The average of 24 numbers is 43. If we subtract a number 'M' from each number, then the average becomes 38. What was the value of M?
questions.solution:
**Given **

Average of 24 numbers = 43

New average when 'M' is subtracted from each number = 38

**Concept used:**

Properties of averages

**Solution:**

⇒ When a constant is subtracted from each number in a set, the average of the set decreases by that constant

⇒ Therefore, the value of M = 43 - 38 = 5

**Therefore, the value of M is 5**

questions.question: Anil alone takes 2 hrs 40 min to complete a work and sumit alone can complete the same work in half time of Anil How much time will be taken by sumit to complete the work?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Anil takes 2 hrs 40 min to complete a work

Sumit completes the work in half the time taken by Anil

**Concept:**

Basic time conversion and division

**Solution:**

⇒ Time taken by Anil = 2 hrs 40 min = 160 min

⇒ Time taken by Sumit = Half of time taken by Anil = 160/2 min

**Therefore, Sumit will take 80 minutes to complete the work **

questions.question: What is that least number that should be added to 478 so that the number obtained becomes exactly divisible by 5, 6, and 12?
questions.solution:
**Given**

The number 478

**Concept used:**

The number should be divisible by the least common multiple (LCM) of 5, 6, and 12

solution**:**

⇒ LCM of 5, 6, and 12 = 60

Please note that 480 is divisible by 60.

⇒ Number to be added = 480 - 478 = 2

**Therefore, 2 should be added to 478 to make it divisible by 5, 6, and 12.**

questions.question: A table is bought for Rs. 2450 and sold for Rs. 2940. The gain percent is:
questions.solution:
**Given**

Cost price = Rs. 2450

Selling price = Rs. 2940

**Formula used:**

Gain percent = [(Selling Price - Cost Price)/Cost Price] × 100

**Solution:**

⇒ Gain = Selling Price - Cost Price = Rs. 2940 - Rs. 2450 = Rs. 490

⇒ Gain percent = (Gain/Cost Price) × 100 = (490/2450) × 100

**Therefore, the gain percent is 0.2 or 20%**

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 28500 is lent out at 6.4% per annum simple interest for 10 years. What will be amount after 10 years?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Principal (P) = Rs. 28500

Rate of interest (R) = 6.4% per annum

Time (T) = 10 years

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest = PRT/100

**Solution:**

⇒ Simple Interest = (28500 × 6.4 × 10)/100

⇒ Total Amount = Principal + Simple Interest

**Therefore, the amount after 10 years will be Rs. 46740**

questions.question: Pipes A and B together can fill a tank in 10 hours. Pipes B and C together can fill the same tank in 12 hours. Pipes A and C together can fill the same tank in 15 hours. In how many hours can pipe B alone fill the same tank?
questions.solution:
**Given**

A and B together can fill a tank in 10 hours

B and C together can fill the same tank in 12 hours

A and C together can fill the same tank in 15 hours

**Formula used:**

For combined work, 1/(time of work) equals to sum of rates of work

**Solution:**

⇒ 1/A + 1/B = 1/10

⇒ 1/B + 1/C = 1/12

⇒ 1/A + 1/C = 1/15

⇒ Adding all three equations we get 2(1/A + 1/B + 1/C) = 1/10 + 1/12 + 1/15

⇒ From which we get 1/B = 2/(1/10 + 1/12 + 1/15) - 1/10 - 1/15

**Therefore, the time taken by pipe B alone to fill the tank is 120/7 hours **

questions.question: P sells a toy to Q at a profit of 40 percent and Q sells it to R at a profit of 10 percent. If R pays Rs. 539 for the toy, then what was the cost price of toy for P?
questions.solution:
**Given**

P sold the toy to Q at 40% profit

Q sold it to R at 10% profit

R paid Rs. 539 for the toy

**Formula used:**

Profit percent = [(Selling Price - Cost Price)/Cost Price] × 100

**Solution:**

⇒ Selling Price of Q to R = Rs. 539

⇒ Cost Price for Q = Selling Price of Q to R / (1 + profit% of Q) = 539/1.1

⇒ Cost Price for P = Cost Price for Q/(1 + profit% of P)

**Therefore, the cost price of the toy for P is Rs. 350 **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 539 = CP of P × 140/100 × 110/100

⇒ CP of P = (539 × 100)/(14 × 11) = Rs. 350

∴ The cost price of the toy for P is Rs. 350.

questions.question: The ratio of speed of three racers is 3 ∶ 2 ∶ 4. What is the respective ratio of time taken by the three racers to cover the same distance?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Ratio of speed of three racers = 3 ∶ 2 ∶ 4

**Concept used:**

The time taken is inversely proportional to the speed

**Solution:**

⇒ Ratio of time = 1/3 ∶ 1/2 : 1/4

**Therefore, the ratio of time taken by three racers is 4 ∶ 6 ∶ 3**

questions.question: HCF of 3/4, 15/16 and 18/5 is:
questions.solution:
**Given**

Numbers are 3/4, 15/16, and 18/5

**Concept used:**

HCF of fractions = HCF of numerators/LCM of denominators

**Solution:**

⇒ HCF of numerators = HCF of 3, 15, 18

⇒ LCM of denominators = LCM of 4, 16, 5

⇒ HCF of fractions = HCF of numerators/LCM of denominators

**Therefore, HCF of 3/4, 15/16 and 18/5 is 3/80.**

questions.question: Let a bag contain 2 kg of sugar and 3 kg of salt. What percent of total is occupied by sugar?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Sugar = 2 kg

Salt = 3 kg

**Formula used:**

Percentage = (Part/Total) × 100

**Solution:**

⇒ Total = Sugar + Salt

⇒ Percentage of sugar = (Sugar/Total) × 100

**Therefore, the percent of total occupied by sugar is 0.4 or 40%**

questions.question: The ratio of the sides of a triangles is 11 ∶ 11 ∶ 4. If the area of triangle is 2sqrt{117} cm², then what is the length of the equal sides?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
Let the common ratio multiplier be x, making the sides of the triangle 11x, 11x, and 4x.

Drawing a perpendicular to the base bisects it, forming right-angled triangles with hypotenuse 11x and base 2x.

Height = √((11x)² − (2x)²) = √(121x² − 4x²) = √(117x²) = x√117.

Area = ½ × Base × Height = ½ × 4x × x√117 = 2x²√117.

Given Area = 2√117 cm² ⇒ 2x²√117 = 2√117 ⇒ x² = 1 ⇒ x = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 11 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of sides = 11 : 11 : 4

Area of triangle = 2√117 cm²

**Formula Used:**

Heron's Formula: Area = √(s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c))

Semi-perimeter, s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2

•

• Base = 4x
**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the sides of the triangle be a = 11x, b = 11x, and c = 4x.

⇒ Semi-perimeter, s = (11x + 11x + 4x) ÷ 2 = 26x ÷ 2 = 13x.

⇒ Applying Heron's Formula for area:

⇒ Area = √(13x × (13x − 11x) × (13x − 11x) × (13x − 4x))

⇒ Area = √(13x × 2x × 2x × 9x)

⇒ Area = √(468x⁴) = √(4 × 117 × x⁴) = 2x²√117

⇒ Equating this with the given area:

⇒ 2x²√117 = 2√117

⇒ x² = 1

⇒ x = 1 cm

⇒ Length of the equal sides = 11x = 11 × 1 = 11 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 11 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Isosceles Triangle Height

In an isosceles triangle, the altitude drawn to the unequal side (base) bisects both the base and the vertex angle, dividing the triangle into two congruent right-angled triangles.

Heron's Formula

Heron's formula computes the area of any triangle directly from its three side lengths: Area = √(s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)), where s is the semi-perimeter.

Direct Area Formula for Isosceles Triangle

An isosceles triangle with equal sides a and base b has the direct area formula: Area = (b ÷ 4)√(4a² − b²).

questions.question: 30 percent of marked price is equal to 50 percent of cost price. If no discount is given, then what will be the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given **

30 percent of marked price is equal to 50 percent of cost price

**Formula used:**

Profit % = (Selling Price - Cost Price)/Cost Price × 100

**Solution:**

⇒ From the given data, derive the relation between marked price and cost price

⇒ Selling Price = Marked Price (since no discount is given)

MP × 30/100 = CP × 50/100

⇒ MP/CP = 5/3

So

SP = 5

Profit% = [(5 - 3)/3] × 100 = 66.67%

**Therefore, the profit percentage when no discount is given is 66.67 percent (option 1).**

questions.question: Find the compound interest (CI) on Rs. 12,600 for 2 years at 10% per annum compounded annually.
questions.solution:
**Given**

Principal (P) = Rs. 12,600

Rate (R) = 10%

Time (T) = 2 years

**Concept used:**

Compound Interest formula

**Solution:**

⇒ CI = P(1 + R/100)² - P

⇒ CI = 12600(1 + 10/100)² - 12600

⇒ CI = 15246 - 12600 = 2646

**Therefore, the compound interest on Rs. 12,600 for 2 years at 10% per annum compounded annually is Rs. 2646 **

questions.question: A train having length 330 meters takes 11 second to cross a 550 meters long bridge. How much time will the train take to cross a 570 meters long bridge?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance (1) = 330 + 550 = 880 m → 11 s.

Total distance (2) = 330 + 570 = 900 m.

Time = (900 × 11) ÷ 880 = 900 ÷ 80 = 45/4 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is (45/4) seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Train length = 330 m, Bridge₁ = 550 m, Bridge₂ = 570 m, Time₁ = 11 s.

Formula Used: Speed = (Length of Train + Length of Object) ÷ Time

 
 Train

• 
 Total Dist = 880 m (Case 1)
 Time taken = 11 seconds

⇒ Total Distance₁ = 330 + 550 = 880 m.

⇒ Speed of train = Total Distance₁ ÷ Time₁ = 880 ÷ 11 = 80 m/s.

⇒ Total Distance₂ = 330 + 570 = 900 m.

⇒ Time₂ = Total Distance₂ ÷ Speed = 900 ÷ 80.

⇒ Time₂ = 45/4 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is (45/4) seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two trains of lengths L₁ and L₂ cross each other, total distance is always L₁ + L₂. Relative speed is S₁ + S₂ (opposite) or S₁ − S₂ (same direction).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Train crossing a stationary point

When a train crosses a pole, tree, or man, the distance covered is equal to the length of the train itself.</p
